Structural biology

Where it binds and what it looks like: crystallization screening, epitope mapping and higher-order structure.

Assays
2
Standard turnaround
15–18 days
Fastest priority slot
9 days

Structural questions usually come later in a program, when you need to understand an epitope, defend a binding mode or explain why one variant behaves differently from another.

We start with a feasibility check: purity, homogeneity and stability of your complex. Only then do we commit to crystallization screens or hydrogen–deuterium exchange, so you don't pay for months of screening on a sample that was never going to cooperate.

Questions this answers

  • Which residues form the epitope?
  • Will the protein or complex crystallize?
  • Does a sequence change alter higher-order structure?
  • Where do two binders overlap?

Sample requirements

Sample requirements for structural biology
Minimum amount2 mg for crystallization; 500 µg for HDX
Purity95% or higher by SDS-PAGE and SEC
Concentration5–20 mg/mL for crystallization
ShippingFrozen in single-use aliquots

What you receive

  • Optimized conditions for any crystal hits
  • HDX uptake plots and protection maps
  • Interpretation call with the structural lead
